behavior.arguments: rdi = struct pointer; fields read: flag byte at [rdi+0x15], count dword at [rdi+0x10], compared dword at [rdi+0x4]. No other argument register is read.
behavior.comparison: signed 32-bit throughout: the count gate uses test + jg (signed), and the fallback uses cmp + setle (signed). The flag byte is zero-extended by movzbl, so the returned byte is 0..255 and the setle low byte is the whole return value.

edges.byte_and_positive_count: byte 5, count 3 -> 5 (short-circuit; the dword comparison is never reached).
edges.byte_nonzero_count_negative: byte 5, count -1 -> dword comparison decides (count gate is signed).
edges.full_byte_range: byte 0xff, count 1 -> 255 (movzbl zero-extends; no stale-high-byte caveat).

behavior.entry_shape: Straight-line gate with two forward branches and one ret; no loop, no call opcode inside the window.
behavior.neighbor_jump: The address-order next window 0x5172c90 (FDE [0x5172c90, 0x5172cb5)) ends with jmp 0x5172c70 at 0x5172cb0: an incoming tail jump into this window. It is not a call, and 0x5172c90 itself is not built here.
behavior.return_rule: If the flag byte is nonzero AND the count dword is positive (signed), return the flag byte. Otherwise return 1 iff dword [rdi+0x4] <= dword [rdi+0x10] (signed), else 0.

caller_fdes.note: Site confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; caller setup immediately before the call is lea 0x8f0(%rbp),%rdi; caller purpose not claimed.
Site confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; caller setup immediately before the call is lea 0x8f0(%r12),%rdi; caller purpose not claimed.
Site confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from the caller FDE start; caller setup immediately before the call is add $0x8f0,%rdi; caller purpose not claimed.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; every site was additionally confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from its caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps (including the neighbor jump from 0x5172cb0), and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.

scout_corrections: The round-12 scout note listed this window (ranked #1) with FDE [0x5172c70, 0x5172c8a), 26 bytes, 6 padding bytes, three direct callers all boundary-confirmed, no naming relocation, and the neighbor 0x5172c90 tail-jumping into it. Every element verified exactly, including the neighbor's jmp 0x5172c70 at 0x5172cb0. No numeric correction to the scout's numbers was needed. One phrasing point is reconciled explicitly: the scout's 'zero calls' describes the window body (no call opcode inside it), while the three direct sites are incoming calls from three caller FDEs — the two statements are about different directions and do not conflict.
